heard: Saturn radiates 2.5 times more energy than it receives. Most people think distant planets are warmed only by sunlight. Deep inside, Saturn's core burns at 11,700 degrees Celsius. Helium condenses high in the hydrogen atmosphere and rains downward. Friction from falling liquid helium creates massive internal heat. This heat engine powers winds reaching 1,800 kilometers per hour. The heat even drives a giant hexagonal storm in its north pole. That internal engine is why Saturn radiates 2.5 times more energy than it than it receives.
